title: Hybrid shadow deploy runtime adaptor notes
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for an experiment: a lightweight runtime adaptor to enable hybrid 'shadow' deployments for model variants and hardware pools. Goal is to let traffic be mirrored (or partially routed) to an alternate serving surface (private/dedicated/experimental) to validate correctness, performance, and cost signals before full rollouts.

Why hybrid shadow?
- We want production traffic characteristics (latency distribution, token mix, prompt shapes) while isolating risk.
- Need to measure P99 degradation, KV cache miss amplification, and incremental cost for a candidate model/hardware combo.
- Prefer a non-invasive surface that plugs into existing ingress routing and telemetry pipeline with minimal schema changes.

High-level requirements (non-exhaustive):
1) Config-driven sampling: per-tenant and global sampling rates, ability to bias by route/model/feature flags.
2) Two shadow modes: mirror (send copy, ignore reply) and mirrored-compare (compare candidate output vs baseline, produce diff events).
3) Fractional routing: route X% requests to candidate surface in addition to mirror; useful when candidate has separate capacity.
4) Lease-based microstate: adaptor must obtain short leases for client-side KV prewarm/priming to avoid polluting production caches.
5) Telemetry hooks and cost accounting: token counts, extra latency, error deltas.
6) Safe failure modes: if candidate errors or times out, baseline path must be unaffected.

Design sketch (runtime adaptor responsibilities):
- Placement: sits as a middleware in ingress (edge/ingress-proxy) or as a sidecar in runtime pool.
- Decision engine: consults routing policy (local cache + control plane) and makes per-request shadowing decision.
- Async forwarding: when in mirror mode, forward candidate request async; for mirrored-compare, forward synchronously with timeout and do lightweight diff.
- Lease manager: request short-lived leases for any candidate cache priming or ephemeral token usage; release eagerly.

API shape (config + control endpoints) - sketch:
- POST /runtime/shadow/evaluate -> body: {"tenant":"string","route":"string","model":"string","mode":"mirror|compare","sample_rate":0.02,"route_fraction":0.1,"ttl_ms":2000}  (returns admission id)
- POST /runtime/shadow/cancel -> body: {"admission_id":"string"}  (cancels a pending evaluation)
- GET  /runtime/shadow/status?admission_id=...  (status: running|succeeded|failed)
- POST /runtime/shadow/lease/acquire -> body: {"scope":"kv-prewarm|plugin-temp","tenant":"string","max_ttl_ms":5000}  (returns lease_id, granted_ttl_ms)
- POST /runtime/shadow/lease/release -> body: {"lease_id":"string"}

Control-plane config (yaml sketch) - this is what the adaptor downloads and caches:
---
policies:
  - id: per-route-prefill-experiment
    selector:
      route_prefix: "/chat/v1"
      tenants: ["beta-team"]
    mode: "compare"
    sample_rate: 0.03
    route_fraction: 0.15
    bake_in_secs: 600   # how long between enabling and starting collection
    telemetry_tags: ["shadow_experiment","prefill_v1"]
    lease_policy:
      scope: "kv-prewarm"
      max_ttl_ms: 3000
---

Runtime decision flow (per request):
1) Evaluate fast selectors (route prefix, tenant, model id) against cached policies.
2) If no match, short-circuit -> no shadow.
3) If match, apply randomized sampling for sample_rate.  Use top-level request salt + consistent hashing for deterministic sampling for sticky sessions.
4) If sampled, consult route_fraction: if route_fraction > 0, route a mirrored fraction of traffic to candidate surface that is capacity-constrained.
5) Acquire required lease(s) (non-blocking best-effort). If lease fail, adapt behavior: for compare mode, still mirror but tag telemetry as "lease-miss".
6) Forward baseline and candidate according to mode. For compare mode, allow candidate timeout <= baseline_timeout*1.5; if candidate tardy, record latency delta but do not affect baseline reply.
7) Produce telemetry event with deltas and store in shadow index for offline analysis.

Telemetry schema (event fields we add):
- admission_id (string)
- policy_id (string)
- tenant, route, model_baseline, model_candidate
- mode, sampled, route_fraction_applied
- baseline_latency_ms, candidate_latency_ms, latency_delta_ms
- baseline_tokens, candidate_tokens, token_delta
- compare_result_status: identical|different|no_candidate|timeout|error
- lease_ids: [ids], lease_grants_ms
- cost_estimate_usd (approx)

Failure & safety modes:
- Candidate errors: swallow and tag event; baseline unaffected.
- Slow candidate: enforce hard cap (candidate_timeout) and attach partial outputs if we want to do delta analysis offline.
- Lease starvation: degrade to purely async mirror and mark telemetry.
- Control-plane disconnect: respect last-known cached policy and switch to fail-open (no shadow) after TTL expiry.

Lease arbitration notes (why leases):
- Some candidate surfaces will prewarm KV caches or initialize plugin runtimes which can pollute or over-allocate shared resources. Leases let us: (a) express ephemeral right to touch prewarm resources, (b) avoid unbounded prewarm storms, (c) account cost per-lease.
- Lease manager SHOULD support two modes: optimistic (best-effort) and strict (block until granted or abort). For this experiment default to optimistic.

Mini-examples:
1) Simple compare invocation (curl pseudocode):
curl -X POST https://ingress/runtime/shadow/evaluate -d '{"tenant":"acme","route":"/chat/v1","model":"gpt-like-7b-xq","mode":"compare","sample_rate":0.05,"route_fraction":0.0,"ttl_ms":120000}'
-> returns admission_id: "shd-20250109-0001"

2) Lease acquire:
POST /runtime/shadow/lease/acquire -> {"scope":"kv-prewarm","tenant":"acme","max_ttl_ms":2500} -> {"lease_id":"lsh-42","granted_ttl_ms":1800}

Operational questions / open items (to resolve in next pass):
- How expensive is synchronous mirrored-compare at 0.05 sample for high throughput routes? Need simulation (token distribution matters).
- Do we need to materialize full outputs for diffs or just distilled assertions (semhash/digest)? Privacy concerns if storing full responses.
- Where to enforce route_fraction? In adaptor or in control plane? Adaptor-local enforcement reduces control-plane churn.
- Metric cardinality: policy_id+tenant+route+model_pair could explode. Consider bucketing or rollup strategy.
- Is it acceptable to re-use existing KV-lease service or add a tiny per-adaptor lease pool?

Sketch: ascii flow diagram

[client] -> [ingress adaptor decision engine] -> baseline -> baseline-pool -> reply -> client
                              |
                              +-> (mirror async) candidate -> candidate-pool -> (store event)
                              +-> (compare sync) candidate -> candidate-pool -> compare -> event -> baseline reply unaffected

Notes-to-self:
- Make the adaptor as stateless as possible; leases and policy cache are the minimal state.
- Keep telemetry tags small; prefer boolean flags + low-cardinality enums.
- Build a simulation harness: replay 24h of captured request headers/prompt-length distribution and run different sample_rate/route_fraction combos to get P50/P95/P99, token deltas, and cost delta estimates.

Next steps (short):
- Prototype lightweight adaptor under runtime/ingress/shadow-adaptor with optimistic lease manager.
- Wire a tiny telemetry sink (shadow-index) and a playground viewer that shows diffs and cost estimates per policy id.
- Run small beta with "platform-internal" tenant and a non-critical route.

Random notes: consider adding a deterministic-sampling toggle so the same session is always shadowed to allow session-level diffs. Also consider a "quiet-mode" that only logs but does not store candidate outputs when privacy mode set for tenant.

----
Edits log: 2025-01-09 initial sketch; 2025-01-14 added lease manager + telemetry schema; 2025-01-22 added control-plane config and API shapes.
